title: Finite generator-relation presentations and their left exact transport
statement:
Let $\mathcal E=\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal C)$ and $\mathcal F=\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal B)$ be categories of set sheaves on small sites [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology], in the containing universes [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $(G_i)_{i\in I}$ be a small family of quasi-compact objects generating $\mathcal E$: every object receives an epimorphism from a coproduct of members of this family. Let $L:\mathcal E\to\mathcal F$ be a finite-limit-preserving left adjoint (with its adjunction as in [def-trf-geometric-morphism]), and suppose every $LG_i$ is coherent [def-trf-coherent-topos]. For every coherent object $A$ of $\mathcal E$, there are finite sets $J,K$, maps $i:J\to I$, $j:K\to I$, and epimorphisms
$$p:P=\coprod_{a\in J}G_{i(a)}\longrightarrow A,\qquad q:Q=\coprod_{b\in K}G_{j(b)}\longrightarrow R=P\times_A P.$$
The object $R$ is quasi-compact. The functor $L$ preserves coproducts and epimorphisms, $LP$ is coherent, $LQ$ is quasi-compact, and $Lq:LQ\to LR$ is an epimorphism onto a quasi-compact object. The canonical comparison $LR\xrightarrow{\sim}LP\times_{LA}LP$ is an isomorphism compatible with both kernel-pair projections. Both finite sets are allowed to be empty; no representability of $R$ is required.

proof.text: By the generating hypothesis choose a small epimorphic family $(G_{i(t)}\to A)_{t\in T}$. Coherence of $A$ implies quasi-compactness [def-trf-coherent-topos], so a finite subset $J\subseteq T$ still covers $A$. Its coproduct map is the required $p:P\to A$, with $i$ the restricted index map. The summands of $P$ are quasi-compact by hypothesis, so $P$ is quasi-compact by clause (3) of [lem-trf-topos-finite-cover-calculus]. Since $A$ is quasi-separated, its defining condition applied to the two maps $p:P\to A$ says that $R=P\times_A P$ is quasi-compact [def-trf-coherent-topos]. Apply the generating hypothesis again, now to $R$, and use its quasi-compactness to select a finite subfamily indexed by $K$. Its restricted index map $j:K\to I$ and coproduct give the required epimorphism $q:Q\to R$. These are arbitrary sheaf morphisms, so this construction never requires $R$ to be representable.

source.place: Tag 00WS (lemma-sheaf-coequalizer-representable), generator cover followed by a cover of the kernel pair; finite extraction is from the definition of quasi-compactness; Tag 0GMQ (lemma-coproduct-quasi-compact).

proof.text: Write $L\dashv U$ for the assumed adjunction [def-trf-geometric-morphism]. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-left-adjoint-preserves-colimits] to discrete small indexing categories: $L$ preserves all coproducts in the containing universes, in particular $LP\simeq\coprod_{a\in J}LG_{i(a)}$ and $LQ\simeq\coprod_{b\in K}LG_{j(b)}$. Epimorphisms are also preserved, directly by right cancellation: if $e:X\to Y$ is epic and $r,s:LY\to Z$ satisfy $r\circ Le=s\circ Le$, their adjoint transposes $\widetilde r,\widetilde s:Y\to UZ$ satisfy $\widetilde r\circ e=\widetilde s\circ e$ by naturality. Epicity gives $\widetilde r=\widetilde s$, and the adjunction bijection gives $r=s$. Thus $Le$ is epic. In particular $Lp$ and $Lq$ are epimorphisms. This argument uses ordinary categorical epimorphisms, without any sectionwise-surjectivity assertion.

source.place: Tag 0038 (lemma-adjoint-exact), part (1), for coproducts; the epimorphism assertion is the displayed elementary adjunction/cancellation argument.

proof.text: Each $LG_i$ is coherent by hypothesis. The finite coproduct assertion of [lem-trf-sheaf-quasicompact-coproduct-calculus], applied in $\mathcal F$, and the coproduct comparisons of step 2 show that $LP$ is coherent. Each $LG_i$ is also quasi-compact by [def-trf-coherent-topos], so clause (3) of [lem-trf-topos-finite-cover-calculus] shows that $LQ$ is quasi-compact. Apply clause (2) of that node to the epimorphism $Lq:LQ\to LR$ from step 2: $LR$ is quasi-compact. Both cited coproduct statements include the empty coproduct, so these arguments impose no nonemptiness condition on $J$ or $K$.

source.place: Tags 0GMP (lemma-image-of-quasi-compact), 0GMQ (lemma-coproduct-quasi-compact); coherent finite sums and the empty cases use the explicitly cited existing extensions.

proof.text: Let $r_1,r_2:R\rightrightarrows P$ be the two projections. The assumed finite-limit preservation [def-trf-geometric-morphism] sends the pullback square defining $R$ to a pullback square with vertex $LR$ and legs $Lr_1,Lr_2$. Its canonical map $c:LR\to LP\times_{LA}LP$ is defined by $\pi_1c=Lr_1$ and $\pi_2c=Lr_2$. Conversely, the pullback property of the image square supplies a unique map $d:LP\times_{LA}LP\to LR$ with $Lr_1d=\pi_1$ and $Lr_2d=\pi_2$. The composites $cd$ and $dc$ have the same two projections as the corresponding identity maps; uniqueness in each pullback gives $cd=1$ and $dc=1$. Thus $c$ is the asserted isomorphism with both required compatibilities. If either finite family chosen in step 1 is empty, the same pullback argument applies without change; finite extraction and the coproduct calculus already covered those choices.

source.place: Universal property of a pullback, applied to the assumed finite-limit-preserving functor; explicit comparison and inverse.

Step 1: quasi-compactness of A (part of coherence in def-trf-coherent-topos) gives a finite subfamily J; clause (3) of lem-trf-topos-finite-cover-calculus makes P quasi-compact; quasi-separatedness of A with B=C=P makes R quasi-compact; a second finite selection gives q. Step 2: the Mathlib leaf lem-weil-pbc-left-adjoint-preserves-colimits (Adjunction.leftAdjoint_preservesColimits) applied to discrete diagrams gives coproduct preservation; it is a generic tool, so its use across units is fine. The epimorphism argument by adjoint transposes is complete. Step 4 is genuinely elementary: the pullback comparison c and its inverse d come from the two universal properties. Sources checked: Stacks sites.tex 00WS (l.2441), whose proof covers F and then its kernel pair; tags 0GMP, 0GMQ and 0038 exist. Small cases checked: Sets with a singleton generator, A initial (J=K=∅), and nonempty A (forces J nonempty, which the statement allows).
